quote: we propose the NDR, a black-box red teaming approach, to generate test cases through disentangling and regulating the veiled success information.
Our approach generates test cases (prompts) that elicit unsafe responses from language models... We evaluate red teaming methods by reporting the corresponding attack success rate (ASR).

Red teaming methods aim to construct test cases (malicious prompts) that would stimulate unsafe model responses, and these cases are crucial for building high-quality datasets for supervised finetuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF).
datasets: Red teaming dataset (conversations between humans and an AI assistant)
outputs: Generated test cases for eliciting unsafe responses

quote: We evaluate red teaming methods by reporting the corresponding attack success rate (ASR)... we measure the diversity (Div.) between raw and generated test cases by reporting the similarity score... BLEU score and BERTScore... fluency (Flu.) by reporting the mean sentence perplexity (PPL.)

We measure the diversity (Div.) between raw and generated test cases by reporting the similarity score. We report the averaged BLEU score and BERTScore. ... we also report the Self‑BLEU of generated test cases. ... we measure the sentence fluency (Flu.) by reporting the mean sentence perplexity (PPL.) calculated by GPT‑2‑large.
We report the averaged BLEU score and BERTScore. BLEU measures the semantics similarity in the form of text, while BERTScore measures the semantics similarity based on latent embeddings.
